record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.context_brief: highest-probability stable matching under lottery uncertainty
record.original_question: Under the lottery model of uncertain preferences, what is the computational complexity of computing a matching with the highest probability of being stable in a Stable Marriage instance?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the Stable Marriage problem with n men and n women. In the classical setting, each agent has a strict linear preference order over the agents of the opposite sex, and a perfect matching M is called stable if there is no man–woman pair (m, w) such that m prefers w to his partner in M and w prefers m to her partner in M.

In the lottery model of uncertain preferences, the input is a probability distribution P_a over strict linear orders over the opposite sex for each agent a, and these distributions are mutually independent. A preference profile is sampled by drawing each agent's preference order independently from its distribution. The stability probability of a perfect matching M is the probability, taken over a random preference profile sampled from these independent distributions, that M is stable.

Problem. Determine the computational complexity of the following decision/search problem: given such a lottery-model instance (the n × n probability distributions, encoded as explicit lists of (linear order, probability) pairs with rational probabilities), compute a perfect matching M* whose stability probability is maximum among all perfect matchings (equivalently, decide, given a rational threshold q, whether some perfect matching has stability probability at least q). In particular, is this problem NP-hard, and does it belong to NP, to PP, or to some other natural complexity class?
artifact.status_search_result: According to the work introducing the lottery model for stable matching with uncertain linear preferences (Aziz, Biró, Gaspers, de Haan, Mattei, Rastegari; Algorithmica 2020), computing a matching with the highest stability probability in the lottery model is explicitly listed as an open problem. It is known to be solvable in polynomial time only in restricted cases (e.g., when only a constant number of agents are uncertain and one side of the market has certain preferences). No subsequent resolution of the general case has been located.

status_evidence.title: Stable Matching with Uncertain Linear Preferences (Algorithmica)
status_evidence.snippet: The complexity of MatchingWithHighestStabilityProbability in the lottery model is unknown, except when only a constant number of agents are uncertain on the same side of the market.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of finding a matching with the highest stability probability under the lottery model is stated as open in general.

status_evidence.title: Stable Matching with Uncertain Linear Preferences (arXiv:1607.02917)
status_evidence.snippet: For each model, we study the computational complexity of computing the stability probability of a given matching as well as finding a matching with the highest probability of being stable.
status_evidence.claim: The paper formulates the problem and leaves the general lottery-model complexity of highest-stability-probability matching unresolved.
